applicability.rationale: The supplied manuscript record contains no submission-format details to assess.
The manuscript explicitly asserts that it is within the declared journal scope.
The record describes outcome selection and delayed disclosure of that rule.
The discussion makes a routine-use representativeness claim from selected records.

evidence_anchor.claim: Only each participant's fastest trial is reported, and the selection rule is disclosed only in the discussion.

remedy.cost_tradeoffs: Requires re-analysis and clearer reporting, but the supplied records are available.
remedy.minimum_action: Disclose the selection rule in the methods and analyze all available trial records, clearly distinguishing that analysis from the selected-record analysis.

findings.scholarly_relevance: Undisclosed outcome selection impedes assessment of whether the reported inference reflects the available records.

evidence_anchor.claim: The discussion treats the fastest-trial estimate as representative of routine use, while an analysis using all trials is not reported.

remedy.cost_tradeoffs: May narrow the routine-use claim if it is not supported by analysis of all available records.
remedy.minimum_action: Assess the routine-use claim using all available trial records and revise the claim to match what that analysis supports.

findings.scholarly_relevance: A representativeness claim based solely on fastest records can overstate relevance to ordinary use.
